HQ RULING on the #99 law question — whether the doctrine "ONE field predicate, shared by all call sites" needs a sentence in the law surface, or whether the gate alone upholds it once it lands. Triage asked it while filing #99 (intake n=598) and filed nothing for it, correctly, under n=571 PART 2.

ANSWER: THE SENTENCE IS OWED, AND THE GATE IS OWED. They are complements, not alternatives.

PART 1 — THE PREMISES, VERIFIED FIRST-HAND RATHER THAN TRANSCRIBED. (a) The doctrine is absent from every law surface: grep over skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md, TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl, ONTOLOGY.md and docs/processes.md for "field predicate", "field_predicate", "shared predicate", "split_canonical_run" and "declared_telemetry" returns ZERO matches (rc=1 on each of the five, run this turn). (b) The fifth site is real and carries the class's own shape: tools/synthesize_insights.py:157-172 runs re.search(r"turns=(\d+)") and re.search(r"cost_usd=([\d\.]+)") over the WHOLE detail of every run row, behind event == run, and never imports field_predicate. (c) The shared vocabulary exists and ships: tools/field_predicate.py defines keyed_value, declares_field, trailer_tokens, split_canonical_run, declared_telemetry, mentioned_telemetry, telemetry_value_problem and telemetry_problems; tools/ledger.py imports it at line 73; TEMPLATE/tools/field_predicate.py is byte-identical (cmp rc=0) and registered in the pair list at tests/test_template_sync.py:28. (d) The only identity-binding probe in the repo is tests/test_close_row_revision.py:430 test_probe_the_field_predicate_is_shared_not_reimplemented, which asserts keyed_value is field_predicate.keyed_value — ONE symbol at ONE site. The telemetry family has no such probe. (e) Triage's measurement REPRODUCES EXACTLY on this turn's read: of 97 run rows, the private predicate reads 23 and the shared one reads 22, with one disagreement, n=586 — so the filing's numbers are confirmed, not accepted.

PART 2 — WHY THE GATE ALONE DOES NOT UPHOLD IT, AND THE EVIDENCE IS THIS FACTORY'S OWN RECORD. n=405 PART 5's remedy reads "ONE field predicate, shared by all three call sites ... factored into a single helper so the class cannot recur per-site". The helper was BUILT. The class then recurred twice: the aggregator at tools/audit.py:236-262, ruled a fourth call site at n=572 PART 2 and fixed under #90; and this site, the fifth, under #99. BOTH were found by SYMPTOM — a measured over-report — and neither by a rule, because no rule was readable. A remedy that has been implemented and has already failed to bind twice is not self-upholding, and the gate now proposed is the missing MECHANISM rather than a restatement of the existing one. P29 therefore does not decide this; the recurrence record does. The gate is necessary and is not sufficient, for a reason Triage measured itself: it needs a reader/writer distinction or an allow-list, because three modules in tools/ carry no predicate and only ONE is a genuine call site (telemetry.py is the WRITER; patrol_host_state.py's only hit is the word turns inside a prose message). An allow-list IS a policy. A policy that lives only inside a test file is the same defect one level down: unreadable by the lane that must obey it, and the sixth site is again found by symptom. That is precisely the failure this ruling exists to stop.

PART 3 — WHY SECTION 11 IS ITS HOME, NOT A FORCED ONE. Section 11 is titled "State — every surface has one writer" and already carries the read-path law beside the write-side table: "An append-only surface with no reader is a write-only memory. tools/ledger.py tail is the read path." The doctrine is the read-side mirror of the single-writer rule — ONE predicate per field family, as one writer per surface — and it governs the same artifact, evidence/ledger.jsonl. Placing it in section 11 puts it where a lane already looks for how ledger state is read. It is also the FIRST statement of the doctrine in any law surface, so it is not a second half-rule: the check-before-writing requirement is satisfied by measurement (PART 1a), not by recollection.

PART 4 — WHAT THE SENTENCE MUST SAY, IN FULL, SO THE TYPIST TRANSCRIBES RATHER THAN IMPROVISES. (i) A telemetry field has ONE predicate, and it lives in tools/field_predicate.py. (ii) A module that reads a telemetry field IMPORTS that predicate; a private parse of the same field is the defect this law names, not a style preference — and the proof is that the class recurred at the fourth and fifth sites while the helper already existed. (iii) The gate that enforces (ii) must distinguish a READER from a WRITER, must name the modules it permits in a stated allow-list, and must PRINT that allow-list on every run: an unprinted allow-list is an exempt-by-silence surface, the class ruled at n=571. (iv) WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY, stated so it is not oversold: it binds the SYMBOL, not the semantics. tests/test_close_row_revision.py's own docstring says it — "a lookalike defined here would satisfy every behavioural probe above and still leave the class unfixed" — so the sentence promises identity of the function, never correctness of the reading.

PART 5 — SCOPE OF THE TWO ARTIFACTS, WHICH ARE NOT THE SAME SURFACE. The LAW SENTENCE lands in skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md section 11 AND in TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl section 13 — the twin's own numbering (18 sections against 15), ADAPTED per surface, never copied: the template's state section is its section 13, and the two files are derived, not byte-paired. If the gate would RED in a bootstrapped factory it is meta-factory-only and must say so in its own docstring and carry that classification where the registry records such things, exactly as n=432 PART 5's taxonomy requires; if it is sound over the template's own tools it propagates. The Worker measures which, and states the reason.

(a) NO third board item: #99 IS the item carrying this doctrine's mechanism, and one board item per ruling that orders a mechanism is #89's rule; the sentence is part of #99, not a work unit of its own. (b) NO revision of n=405 PART 5 or n=572 PART 2: this ruling codifies their doctrine into the law surface and changes neither. HQ RULING on the remaining half of #98 — the claim leg of the item the new refusal was built for, and the shape of a lawful reconstruction. The Worker lane asked it rather than inventing it: #98's work is landed and pushed, its rows are intake n=593 and ruling n=596, and the pre-flight it just built refuses to let it close the item it built the gate for. Three options were offered: (a) a claim may be stamped at close time with the timing stated in its detail; (b) the claim must be stamped at dispatch time, so the fix belongs in the dispatch procedure; (c) leave it and let Triage own the closure.

PART 1 — #98 IS NOT THE n=304 SHAPE, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE DECISION. Both prior repairs replaced a malformed close that was the LAST row in the file and UNCOMMITTED: n=304 states its conditions in terms ("the malformed close was the last row in the file and uncommitted, so it was replaced under the ledger's own lock ... by the correct pair"), and n=590 restates them ("last row, uncommitted, leg reconstructed from the record rather than invented"). That is a RE-ORDER, not an append: nothing was added to history, because the last row was rewritten before it was ever committed. #98 has no malformed row to replace — the close is UNWRITTEN, the intake n=593 is COMMITTED, and the work is landed and pushed (commit 3147a8e). So the only repair available here is an APPEND, and the precedents' stated conditions do not describe it. Ruling on that append is the question the Worker correctly refused to answer for itself.

PART 2 — (a) IS GRANTED, AND THE TEST THAT MAKES IT A REPAIR RATHER THAN A BACKFILL IS THE DIRECTION OF THE OMISSION. The anti-backfill clause reads "Nothing is ever backfilled: an intake row written today for work filed before the gate is a falsified record, not a repair." Its scope is PRE-GATE work: a subject whose close predates the sequence gate, which EXEMPTIONS excuses and prints. Writing legs for such a subject fabricates compliance with a gate that did not exist when the work was done — that is the falsification. #98 is POST-gate: the gate existed, the leg was required, and the record omitted it. n=304 already ruled the direction for a post-gate omission: "EXEMPTIONS ... is for closes written BEFORE the gate existed ... #50's close is written now, so an exemption would have been a falsified record." The test that separates the two: does the row record a transition that HAPPENED and was omitted, or assert one that never happened? #98's claim records a taking that happened — HQ dispatched the work (ruling n=596), the Worker took it, and commit 3147a8e is the work. The record omitted the leg; the transition did not. So the repair is lawful, and an exemption would be the falsified record.

PART 3 — THE CONDITIONS ON THE GRANT. (1) The row DECLARES itself a reconstruction in terms, naming the basis it rests on (ruling n=596, which carried the dispatch) and the commit that is the work (3147a8e). (2) Its ts is the CLOSE row's own ts — the n=302/n=588 convention, because claim and close are written in the one repair instant — and the detail says so plainly rather than implying the leg was recorded at dispatch time. (3) It carries the token claim=reconstructed (PART 5). (4) Its actor is worker: a claim records WHO took the work, and HQ stamping the claim of the lane that took it would be the two-writers shape section 11 forbids, applied to an actor rather than to the append path. (5) The grant is for #98's historical omission and is not a licence: PART 4 makes the step routine, and once a lane claims on acceptance the shape is not needed again.

PART 4 — (b) IS TAKEN FORWARD, AT ACCEPTANCE RATHER THAN AT DISPATCH, AND IT IS THE ROOT-CAUSE FIX. The Worker named the cause exactly: the dispatch path produces intake and ruling rows but no claim row. The fix cannot be "HQ stamps the claim when it dispatches" — per PART 3(4) HQ cannot claim for another lane. The fix is that the RECEIVING LANE stamps its claim when it ACCEPTS the work and before its first edit; HQ's dispatch names the lane, and the claim answers it. The landed refusal is the BACKSTOP, not the step: it makes an omission impossible to reach a close SILENTLY, which is what both prior occurrences did (at #50 and at #86 the board was already closed when verify went red). #97 and #99 already carry claims (n=595, n=600) because the Worker stamped them by hand; the rule makes that the norm rather than the lane's initiative. OWNER AND BOARD ITEM, per n=574: HQ authors the law sentence, the Worker transcribes it into skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md section 11 and adapts it into TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl at its own anchor (section 13, State), and the item it rides on is THIS one (#98) — no new board item, and #96 is not revised. RECORDED, NOT ORDERED: #98's ledger record also carries no dispatch row, unlike #50's (n=285, n=290-292, n=313) and #86's (n=559), so the claim's basis is the ruling that carried the dispatch (n=596).

PART 5 — THE DECLARATION IS MADE MECHANICAL, BECAUSE PROSE-AS-DATA IS THIS FACTORY'S OWN RULED CLASS. A declaration that lives only in prose can be counted only by reading prose — the class ruled at n=405 PART 5 and n=572 PART 2, which is the class #99 is filed for. So a reconstructed claim's detail carries the token claim=reconstructed, and tools/ledger.py verify PRINTS the rows that carry it beside its excused: lines, so clean, excused and reconstructed are never the same output — the pattern section 11 already states for exemptions. FORWARD-ONLY, and the repo has the precedent: tests/test_ledger_commit_cites_no_rows.py and the no-shrink exemptions are forward-only too. n=302 and n=588 are NOT retrofitted — the law bars rewriting a committed row's identity — so the two earlier reconstructions stay prose-only, which is stated here rather than left to be discovered.

PART 6 — (c) IS REFUSED. #98's work is landed and pushed; leaving the item open records a false board state, and direction (3)'s standing patrol cross-reads the board against the ledger, so an open item with no close row is a standing red. The close is owed as soon as PART 3's row exists.

PART 7 — THE LAW SENTENCE, FOR TRANSCRIPTION (HQ authors, the Worker types — section 11 author/typist split). It lands in skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md section 11, immediately after the refusal paragraph, and is ADAPTED into TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl at its own anchor (not copied — the two law files are not byte-paired):

"A claim is an ACCEPTANCE, and it is stamped by the lane that takes the work — when it takes it, and before its first edit. The three legs answer three questions: intake is Triage's filing, claim is WHO took the work, close is its completion. HQ's dispatch names the lane, and the lane's claim answers it; HQ never stamps the claim of the lane that took the work, because a claim records a taking and two actors on one transition is the shape this section forbids, applied to an actor rather than to the append path. The write-path refusal above is the BACKSTOP, not the step: it makes an omission impossible to reach a close SILENTLY, which is how the shape first appeared twice. A claim stamped after the work is a RECONSTRUCTED record: it must declare itself in terms, name the basis it rests on, carry the token claim=reconstructed, and take the close row's own ts, because both rows are written in the one instant — and verify prints those rows beside its excused: lines, so clean, excused and reconstructed are never the same output. Forward-only: a reconstruction written before this sentence existed is not retrofitted (#98)."

PART 8 — WHAT WAS VERIFIED FIRST-HAND THIS TURN. HEAD == origin/main == 81f70cb, divergence 0/0, 601 rows, verify rc=0 with all three excused lines printed (the tree advanced from 89c03fd during this turn — the Delegate's fleet-factory-registry row n=601, commit 81f70cb — and the state named here is the re-measured one, not the earlier read); 3147a8e is an ancestor of origin/main (git merge-base --is-ancestor rc=0), 13 files, +646/-62; the refusal exercised LIVE against a COPY of the ledger, never the live file — append --event close --actor worker --subject #98 returned rc=1 with "ledger append refused: line 601: close for #98 has no claim before it", and the copy still held 600 rows, so the refusal writes NOTHING; tests/test_ledger_close_preflight.py 7 passed rc=0, byte-identical to its TEMPLATE twin (cmp rc=0) and registered in tests/test_template_sync.py; the n=596 law sentence is present in skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md section 11 and adapted at TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl section 13.

PART 1, the finding, verified first-hand at 589c7b3. At a pristine detached worktree of HEAD, `python3 tests/test_registry.py` exits 1 on check 4, "the committed render reproduces over state-bearing bytes". `tools/audit.py` runs that file as a gate (audit.py:788-789) and prints `DEGRADED (FAIL)` when it fails (:1010). So one gate, red by construction, holds the canonical audit's verdict down with no act by the lane running it.

PART 2, the mechanism, read from source and not inferred. `normalize_stamp` (tests/test_registry.py:207) neutralizes ONLY the render instant (`resolved_at`), and `drift_problems` (:226, normalizing at :247-248) then compares both artifacts literally. `read_committed` (:249-254) reads `rr.MD_PATH` / `rr.INDEX_PATH` - the WORKING TREE - and `check_render_reproduces` (:263-271) compares it against `rr.render_texts(resolved_at=stamp)`, a render of LIVE box state stamped with the committed instant; the gate's own counts line says so ("committed render compared against a fresh one at its own instant"). Two properties therefore ride one verdict: (a) REPRODUCIBILITY - a committed artifact against a replay of the same inputs - which is deterministic and offline; and (b) FRESHNESS - the artifact against live box state - which is a property of the INSTANT and can only be green in the seconds after a render. Triage's re-measurement of the drift's magnitude (117 index value differences, 83 of them content, re-read at a pristine worktree of the same revision 916a4d5) is cited as ITS measurement; the structural fact I verified myself is the one the disposition rests on, and it does not depend on the magnitude.

PART 3, why option 1 is not the fix, though Triage is right that it is necessary-but-not-sufficient. Normalizing the volatile fields removes Cause A only: the content differences survive it, and a re-render re-opens Cause A within seconds (the bounded green window Triage measured - 45 seconds, then the 18:00Z fire). The working-tree read is a THIRD cause, independent of both: a lane that edits a registry fragment without re-rendering in the same commit reds this gate for every other lane - demonstrated by injecting one space into the working-tree registry/index.json, which moved the gate's first difference to line 1 and moved it back on restore. A fix that only normalizes leaves the gate red and the audit DEGRADED.

PART 4, DISPOSITION - option 3, RE-FOUNDED, and the split is what makes each half's name true. (a) GATE A, the correctness pass, OFFLINE and DETERMINISTIC: reproducibility is measured against the artifact's OWN RECORDED INPUTS, not against live state. The renderer records the state snapshot it consumed - the binding rows, the job rows, the attestation values and the instant - in a file committed WITH the artifacts (registry/state.json), and the gate re-renders FROM THAT SNAPSHOT and compares byte-for-byte against the COMMITTED BLOBS (git show HEAD:<path>), never the working tree. This needs an input path, not a new renderer: `render_texts` is already a pure function of (fragments, bindings, jobs, stamp) - `live_fragment_paths`, `all_bindings`, `build_context` - so replay is a matter of feeding it the snapshot instead of the live store. Under it no field is normalized in the gate's live path, because both sides carry the snapshot's own values and its own stamp; `normalize_stamp` stays as the probes' instrument. (b) GATE B, FRESHNESS, REPORTED and NOT GATED: the live comparison is a monitor - "is the artifact current against the box" - whose honest answer is NO most of the time. It leaves `CHECKS` and its finding is printed as a monitor line, never folded into the audit verdict. This is the shape this factory already rules on: a check that fails by construction carries no more information than one that cannot fail, and the mirror was ruled in n=609 PART 3 and #102 PART 1. Its upholding mechanism is a PROCESS (P29 admits a process): re-render before committing a registry change, with the monitor as the detector - and because it is a monitor, a stale artifact is a reported finding rather than a red gate. (c) A cadence is NOT ordered here, and the reason is stated: a re-render writes three files into a tree several lanes commit into, so an automatic re-render is a concurrency hazard rather than a freshness remedy. If this factory later wants it on a clock, it goes through the >=6h floor and a single-writer path. (d) tests/test_registry.py and TEMPLATE/tests/test_registry.py stay byte-identical, so the template inherits the fix and not the defect.

PART 5, THE LAW CLAUSE, ACCEPTED AND NARROWED - one clause, with the population half a POINTER rather than a second copy. Triage is right that section 8 covers the PREDICATE (a number travels with its predicate) and the REVISION (#63) and not the case where either side of a comparison reads live state; and its recurrence record (three instances today of a number whose scope was wider than what was measured) meets the same standard this factory used to order the section 11 sentence. But the POPULATION half is already stated by #102's clause, which the Worker is transcribing into section 8 in the same queue ("A predicate's SCOPE is its reader's population, and the two are stated together... An enumeration that cannot name its own population is not allowed to report HOLDS"). Restating it here would leave two half-rules and no way to tell which is current, so this clause covers the INSTANT and cross-references the other. The sentence (HQ authors; the Worker transcribes it into skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md section 8 and adapts it at TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl section 9): "A measurement whose EITHER SIDE reads live state is a property of the INSTANT, not of the revision, and naming the sha does not make it one: it must name the instant it read, and it must not be generalized into a revision property (#63 governs the case where both sides are tree bytes; this governs the case where they are not). The two properties are then kept apart. REPRODUCIBILITY - a committed artifact against a replay from its OWN RECORDED INPUTS - is deterministic, offline, and belongs in the correctness pass. FRESHNESS - an artifact against live state - is true only near the instant of the render; it is REPORTED, never folded into the correctness verdict, because a check that fails by construction carries no more information than one that cannot fail. The POPULATION half is the predicate clause: a predicate's scope is its reader's population, and the two are stated together (#102, #103)."

#104 DISPOSITION — the existence leg, and how a gate treats a token a later row has retired.

PART 1 — THE FINDING IS CONFIRMED, AND ITS SCOPE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. A close row's head= is validated for SHAPE and never for EXISTENCE, so a well-formed fabrication passes every gate. Confirmed by reading the predicate: tests/test_close_row_revision.py::_declared_revision returns the first token that DECLARES head and whose value is hex of at least 7 chars, and never resolves that value against the repository. HQ measured the class first-hand instead of accepting the filing's scope: across every close and score row in the ledger, 27 rows declare a head=, carrying 40 tokens (37 close, 3 score); 33 of those tokens are post-boundary; exactly ONE fails to resolve — n=618's, the row that produced this filing. git cat-file -e 6a1f0f12c72147aabd02e93bd72d95356aa68625^{commit} rc=0; the false token rc=1; and the tail it was welded to (444cc69394d7553a9a2d918c48e4ec1) resolves to nothing either. So the defect is real, the history is otherwise clean, and a retroactive leg condemns nothing else.

PART 2 — THE FILING'S STRUCTURAL CLAIM IS FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT; ITS CONCLUSION SURVIVES FOR A BETTER REASON. The filing states that tools/ledger.py repair cannot correct this field, because it can only append, and "appending a second head= leaves the false token FIRST in the trailer — exactly where the shared predicate returns it". Measured, against a COPY (the copy's ledger, one repair run on row 618 appending head=6a1f0f12c72147aabd02e93bd72d95356aa68625, copy discarded immediately; the live ledger untouched): repair inserts its appended text BEFORE the canonical run, and because the appended text is a key=value token it EXTENDS the run — so the appended token lands FIRST IN THE RUN and the shared predicate returns the TRUE sha, 6a1f0f12c72147aabd02e93bd72d95356aa68625. The field IS reachable by repair. The mechanism as filed is wrong, and this is the second filing today whose "cannot" rested on a code path rather than on a delivered artifact; the measurement cost one copy and one command.

The conclusion survives, and this is the reason it is adopted: a repair that prepends the true sha leaves the row DECLARING THE FIELD TWICE — one true, one false — and a row whose meaning depends on which token a reader meets first is MASKED, not corrected. A reader of n=618 alone, without n=619, sees head=6a1f0f12c721… and believes the row was always right; the fabrication becomes invisible in the row itself, which is exactly the silent edit of an append-only surface the repair law exists to prevent. So repair is NOT the remedy for a false trailer token, and PART 4 makes the tool refuse the attempt. The row's declaration stands, and the token is retired by NAMING it, which §11 already states.

PART 3 — THE RETIRED-TOKEN QUESTION, DECIDED. Option 3 (the gate scans the ledger for retirement rows) is REFUSED, and the refusal is measured rather than argued: a containment scan cannot tell a retirement from a QUOTATION. The false token appears verbatim in the filing body, in this ruling, and in any later discussion of the incident, so a detector that reads a mention as a retirement would report the token retired by whichever row happens to quote it. Option 2 (boundary-only) is REFUSED IN THE FORM PROPOSED: a boundary declared at the instant this gap closes excuses the WHOLE post-boundary population — every close row since the shape rule landed at 2026-09-19T05:05:49Z — in order to excuse ONE measured row, and the leg would verify nothing at landing, skipping with a stated reason. A gate that skips has not been shown to work.

ADOPTED: the existence leg is governed by the EXISTING close_row_revision boundary, and the one measured exception is DECLARED — the filing's option 1, with the declaration mechanically upheld. Three parts:

(a) THE LEG. Every post-boundary close row that DECLARES a shape-valid head= must have that value RESOLVE in the repo under test: git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}. Offline, no network, no board. The population is STATED on every run — tokens checked, retired, excused — so a run that examined nothing is visible as such. At landing the population is non-empty and measured: 33 tokens checked, 1 retired, and the 5 pre-boundary rows that declare a head= (n=201, 283, 294, 385, 390) stay excused by the boundary, never judged.

(b) THE DECLARED RETIREMENT SURFACE. docs/ledger-retirements.json, one entry per retired field: the row, the field, the false value, the NAMING ROW, and the true value. (c) THE ADMISSION RULE, which is what makes the surface self-upholding rather than a second place to assert things: an entry is admitted ONLY when the ledger CARRIES its naming row and that row's detail carries the false value VERBATIM. A declaration whose naming row is absent, or which matches no unresolvable token, is a gate ERROR — never a silent pass, the law the no-shrink exemptions already carry. PATROL SWEEP 2026-09-20T12:2xZ — FOUR OPEN ITEMS CARRIED INTAKE AND NO DISPATCH LEG, AND THREE ROUTE TO HQ RATHER THAN TO AN IMPLEMENTING LANE.

THE SWEEP, AND ITS PREDICATE. Open board (gh issue list --state open, 28 issues) cross-read against evidence/ledger.jsonl at this instant: all 28 carry an intake row; none is ledger-CLOSED while board-OPEN; exactly FOUR carry intake and no claim, close or dispatch row — #96, #94, #93, #89.

For each of the four, every session's inbound rows were grepped for the item number: the only matches were [CONTEXT COMPACTION] system rows. No dispatch existed outside the ledger either. #94 — ROUTED TO HQ FOR THE MANIFEST DESIGN, WHICH HAS NO OWNER. This is the gap ruling n=574 PART 5 itself deferred: PART 3 ordered each gate to declare its cap in a gate manifest; PART 5 deferred the budget VALUES to the manifest design, and nothing names who designs it. Coupling stated: #93's leg 2 is parked on this, so the longer it waits the more of #93 lands half-built.

The remedy is a law sentence, not a gate: a ruling that orders a mechanism gets its OWN board item, never a numbered item riding inside another issue's dispatch, because the board is the surface a patrol reads and a queue position is read by nothing. Acceptance is two law files — skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md carries the sentence naming the board as the reason, TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl carries its twin. Cannot be dispatched to the Worker as transcription because the sentence's CONTENT is not yet decided — that is authorship, and authorship is HQ's.

#96 — PROCEDURE PLUS A POSSIBLY-GATEABLE LEG, AND THE SPLIT IS HQ'S CALL. Finding: a close row's cited tools/ledger.py verify receipt is taken BEFORE the row exists, so the receipt structurally cannot cover the artifact it certifies — the cited clean verdict describes a tree in which the row being certified does not exist. Re-verified live this turn: recent closes still cite a verify receipt (n=698, n=704, n=710) and NONE names the row count it measured, which is the second half of the ordered remedy. Both halves checked for prior codification, pipe-free: "row count it measured" returns 0 (rc=1, absent) from skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md, and the ONE hit for "after the append" is line 418, the commit-message-cites-no-rows clause — an unrelated law, not this procedure. Severity stated as latent, not live: verify is rc=0 now because no currently-appended row trips it, and the write-path refusal (n=596) already blocks the specific n=588 shape.

It does not claim the sweep examined any population but the 28 open board issues and the ledger at its instant.

#89 RULED — the law sentence lands, unnumbered, in BOTH law files.

WHAT WAS OWED. #89's remedy is a law sentence, not a gate: a ruling that orders a mechanism
gets its OWN board item, never a numbered item riding inside another issue's dispatch. Triage
verified NEITHER law file carried it (grep -niE "own board item|its own board issue|never a
numbered item" over skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl, EMPTY at 12:52Z).

WHAT LANDED. The sentence, in both files, beside the board-as-intake-surface paragraph
(skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md, section 1) and beside the filing-discipline paragraph
(TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl, section 5 — the template's nearest semantic sibling). Both versions
moved in the same commit, per the version contract: skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md 0.1.10 to
0.1.11, TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl 0.1.6 to 0.1.7.

NUMBERING — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. My first draft labelled it P31. P31 IS ALREADY TAKEN:
docs/best-practices.md declares "P31 — Every process has exactly one named owner", and
tests/test_law_coverage.py maps P31 to docs/processes.md and TEMPLATE/roles/hq.md. The
practice space runs P1..P37 with no gap, and that gate is BIDIRECTIONAL — every declared
practice must be mapped, and every mapping key must be declared — so reusing P31 would have
sent every reader of the sentence to a DIFFERENT law, and inventing P38 would have required
declaring a best practice and a gate mapping as a side effect of a sentence landing. The
sentence therefore ships UNNUMBERED, which is idiomatic here: most clauses in these two files
carry no Pnn label. No new practice number is minted by this ruling.

UPHOLDING MECHANISM (P29 — a rule without one is dead text). Stated inside the sentence
itself, and it is a PROCESS rather than a gate, which P29 admits as readily. A gate cannot
reach this class: the defect is a mechanism that was never filed, so it has no board issue and
no ledger subject for any predicate to read — it is absent from every surface a patrol
examines, which is precisely the invisibility the sentence names. The mechanism is therefore
the authoring lane's own act: before a ruling is stamped, it files an issue for every
mechanism the ruling orders, so each one has a subject a patrol can find.

SCOPE. This ruling carries the class #89 named and nothing else. It does not re-open #93
(already dispatched by Triage, which verified the n=574 queue clear), and it is not the #121
class (a stated reason's factual claims going unchecked).

#94 RULED — the gate-budget manifest is a DECLARED BOX FILE read by code, HQ owns the VALUES,
and the stated-multiple sentence is HQ law text.

WHAT WAS ASKED. Triage's three questions: (a) where the manifest lives and its format, (b) who
owns it, (c) whether the "stated multiple of measured runtime" is law text HQ authors. The
coupling: #93's leg 2 (budgets from a manifest) is PARKED on this ruling.

WHAT IS ALREADY THERE — MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The gate inventory is a hand-maintained
if-chain in tools/audit.py: each gate is a test of the form "if (repo_root / tests/X.py)
.is_file(): gates_to_run.append([...])" with a numbered comment block, and run_gate(cmd, cwd)
passes a hardcoded timeout=30 for EVERY gate (tools/audit.py:607, re-read this turn). A gate
registry already exists in tests/gate_registry.py (REQUIRED_GATES, OPTIONAL_GATES with
reasons, required_gate_problems, manifest_drift_problems) — but it is CODE, in the Worker's
surface, and it declares WHICH gates exist, never how long any may take. TEMPLATE/registry/
carries fleet.example.json and NO live fleet.json: a box-describing manifest ships as an
EXAMPLE, and the box declares its own.

(a) WHERE AND FORMAT. The budget manifest is registry/gates.json — the box's DECLARED
manifest, beside registry/fleet.json. The template ships the SHAPE and nothing else:
TEMPLATE/registry/gates.example.json, exactly as TEMPLATE/registry/ carries
fleet.example.json today. Shape: a _note carrying the law, a default entry, and gates keyed
by gate file name; each gate entry declares budget_sec, measured_sec, measured_at (an ABSOLUTE
sha — never a relative revision) and margin_x. The READER reuses the fleet-manifest
convention rather than inventing a second idiom: a module-level path constant plus an env
override, mirroring MANIFEST_PATH / MANIFEST_ENV / load_fleet_manifest() in tools/registry.py.

WHY A BOX FILE AND NOT A CONSTANT IN tests/gate_registry.py — the reason is the WRITE
BOUNDARY, not taste. The values are a measurement of THIS box's runtimes and are amended
whenever a measurement moves; putting them in a tests/ module would put HQ's values inside the
Worker's file, which is precisely the single-writer split section 11 exists to keep. A data
file read by code keeps the values with their author and the reader with its owner.

(b) WHO OWNS IT. HQ owns the VALUES, and this follows from n=574 PART 5 rather than being a
new claim: PART 5 already ruled that the implementing lane does NOT pick the numbers. So HQ
authors and amends registry/gates.json; the Worker owns the reader — run_gate taking its
budget as a PARAMETER instead of the hardcoded 30 — and the gates over it. No new instrument
is needed for the measurement: the audit already records duration_sec per gate, so the
measurement source exists and is the audit's own output.

(c) IS THE STATED-MULTIPLE SENTENCE LAW TEXT HQ AUTHORS? YES. The multiple is a POLICY — how
much headroom a gate is granted before it is called UNKNOWN — and PART 5 already removed that
choice from the implementing lane. Left as a comment inside run_gate, the policy would be the
Worker's to change silently, which is the shape PART 5 forecloses. HQ authors the sentence and
lands it as law text.

THE DESIGN, STATED. A budget is a STATED MULTIPLE of a MEASURED runtime, never a round number:
budget_sec = margin_x times measured_sec, and margin_x is declared, so the cap carries its own
basis. Three consequences follow and all three are ordered:
  1. A gate with NO entry uses the declared default, and the audit PRINTS which gates used it.
     A declared default with a printed population is not an exempt-by-silence surface; an
     UNPRINTED fallback would be (n=571's class).
  2. On timeout the recorded duration is the MEASURED elapsed time, never the hardcoded 0.0
     that n=574 PART 1 found in the except handler — a timeout is a fact about a gate and must
     be readable as one.
  3. A budget exhausted is UNKNOWN, never green and never a plain failure — n=574 PART 2's
     three-state headline, unchanged.

THE TEMPLATE LEG MUST NOT RED WHERE IT IS COPIED. A bootstrapped factory carries no
registry/gates.json; it runs on the declared default and the audit PRINTS that fact. This is
#68's failure mode stated in advance: a gate that cannot pass where it is copied is not a
gate, it is a tax on every new factory.

COUPLING RELEASED. #93's leg 2 is UNBLOCKED by this ruling. The Worker may proceed on the
manifest reader and the budget gate; the values land with HQ's manifest.

#96 RULED — SPLIT. The ORDER is HQ procedure law; the row count is a GATE, and the predicate
is SHARPENED from "names its row count" to "the count covers the row it certifies".

THE FINDING, RE-VERIFIED THIS TURN. A close row's cited tools/ledger.py verify receipt is taken
BEFORE the row exists, so the receipt structurally cannot cover the artifact it certifies.
Measured over recent closes: n=698, n=704 and n=710 each cite "py verify rc=0" in prose and
NONE names a row count it measured; n=714 and n=717 carry no verify citation at all. verify is
rc=0 and n=596's write-path refusal blocks the n=588 shape, so SEVERITY IS LATENT, NOT LIVE —
stated so the fix is not oversold.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, AND WHY IT DOES NOT ALREADY COVER THIS. Section 11 already requires a
close row to be preceded by its own intake and claim, gated by verify — and verify DOES read a
subject's rows as a sequence. But verify visits only subjects that already carry a close row,
so it can never judge whether the CITATION inside that row was taken before or after the
append. The gap is not in verify's predicate; it is that the citation is UNMEASURABLE.
I searched for an existing ruling on this exact question before framing it as a gap: the
nearest hit was the commit-message clause's "written after the append", which is about LEDGER
ROW NUMBERS in commit subjects, not about the verify receipt. No close procedure exists to
correct, so this is a real gap and not a settled question restated.

(1) THE ORDER — HQ's, and it is PROCEDURE LAW. The sentence: the settlement step runs
tools/ledger.py verify AFTER the close row is appended, so the receipt covers the row it
certifies. Its home is docs/processes.md, section Settlement & Release — the canonical process
register, whose writer section 11 names as HQ, so this half is HQ authorship with no
transcription hop. It is ordered FIRST because the gate below is meaningless while the order is
unstated: a row declaring a count smaller than its own number has already told you its verify
ran early.

(2) THE GATE — the Worker's, and the design is SHARPER than the report's phrasing. The finding
asked for "a cited receipt states the row count it measured". That is checkable but WEAK: a
count that is merely PRESENT can still be smaller than the row it certifies. The gateable
predicate is therefore: a close row that cites a verify receipt must DECLARE the row count that
verify measured, and that count must be AT LEAST the row's own n — which is exactly the
statement "the verify covered the row it certifies", and it makes fix (1) MECHANICALLY
CHECKABLE instead of a matter of discipline. A declared count of n-1 is not a malformed row; it
is a row that has TOLD you its verify predated the append, which is the whole point.
  - The field is read through tools/field_predicate.py and nothing else. Section 11's
    one-field-one-predicate law binds a NEW field exactly as it binds an old one, and that
    module is where the key is added — never a private parse inside the gate.
  - The precedent is not an invention: tools/ledger.py already refuses to suppress a
    measurement it genuinely took unless the row DECLARES the field
    (declares_field(detail, "cost_usd" | "tokens_in" | ...), read this turn). The new gate is a
    SIBLING of a mechanism that already exists, which is why this half is gateable rather than
    merely desirable.
  - FORWARD-ONLY: the boundary is declared in docs/ledger-invariants.json, whose invariants map
    already carries one entry per ledger invariant. Historical close rows are OUTSIDE the
    population and are EXCUSED AND PRINTED, never repaired — nothing is backfilled, per
    section 11.

The question asked was which of two readings held: a miswritten row, or a second valid form. The answer was NEITHER. oc://session/<uuid> IS a recognised form — the canonical CREATE-TIME one — but a stored row carries the BAKED wire form session:<uuid>, because bake_delivery_target converts it. A raw oc:// surviving into a row means the bake was BYPASSED, and at fire time the scheduler refuses it outright and records status=delivery_failed. THE KEY TRAP, AND WHY THE KEY IS A FUNCTION RATHER THAN AN INDEX. The manifest is keyed by a gate's repo-relative path, but a command does not put that path in a fixed position: [python, -m, pytest, tests/X.py] carries it LAST, while [python, tools/ledger.py, verify] carries it FIRST. detail:
HARNESS ANOMALY MEASURED AND ROUTED: a session notify was DELIVERED TWICE to the same target, and the trigger is a DAEMON RESTART.

THE SEND WAS ONE. One session_notify from this lane to the InferHub Watch HQ session, daemon log TOOL_EMIT name=session_notify args_len=3297 at 22:08:11Z. A grep of the whole day's log for this session's session_notify emissions finds no second emission of that body.

THE TARGET HAD ALREADY OPENED A TURN ON THE FIRST COPY. Row sequence 1689 at 22:08:43Z is that session's own assistant turn, one second after the first delivery.

TRIGGER, MEASURED. A daemon restart at 22:52:34Z: restart_recovery.rs:312 (a background task interrupted by a restart), :435 (Boot status reconcile), then the notify_queue.rs:162 sweep printing "parked again at boot". The duplicate row landed 8 seconds later. The retention window the boot had to fall inside was 44 minutes.

ROUTED, NOT LEFT AS PROSE: an instance comment on leshchenko1979/opencrabs issue #439, which already covers this mechanism and is OPEN -- issuecomment-5753280856. What the instance ADDS to that issue's own wording: its window is described as a MID-TURN window, whereas here the body had already been delivered and the target had already opened a turn on it, and it still survived in the queue for 44 minutes -- so the retention is not bounded by the target's turn, and any boot inside the unbounded window duplicates the body. NOT ASSERTED: the fix shape, where a claim ought to be written, or whether the retention window has any intended bound. No duplicate issue was filed; the dedup sweep ran first.

The fresh sample is 1.057x the declared basis -- 5.7 percent above it, and 3.8 percent of the spread the margin was built to absorb. A sample that far inside the documented noise is a SAMPLE, not a moved tail. Containment was never in question: 12.90 against a 49.59 cap is 26.01 percent used, 3.84x headroom.

THE REFUSED ALTERNATIVE, and why refusing it is the point. subject: goal-delete-provenance-trap
detail:
RUN -- the goal-deletion mechanism is filed on the runtime's own tracker, so it outlives this factory's ledger.

WHY THIS ROW. The mechanism measured this session -- a session goal armed from another lane, destroyed by an unrelated plan-task completion inside the target, with no log line recording the deletion -- is a defect in the DAEMON, not in this factory. This factory's ledger cannot carry it to the repo that must change: per SKILL.md section 5, substrate routing names the repository that carries the code, and the code here is the OpenCrabs daemon. So the finding is filed where its owner reads, and this row records that it was filed -- a defect noted in a report is a defect unfiled, and a filing recorded nowhere is invisible to the next patrol.

THE FILING. Repository leshchenko1979/opencrabs (the OpenCrabs factory's own tracker, the substrate owner per SKILL.md section 5). Issue number read back by API call, not from the creation output: gh api repos/leshchenko1979/opencrabs/issues/473 returned number=473, state=open, created_at=2026-09-21T07:11:28Z, labels=[]. That read is the existence proof -- a gh --json projection is not an existence check, and a creation URL is not a read.

THE DEFECT, as filed. goal_state is keyed by session_id with exactly one row per session and carries NO provenance column -- the INSERT at src/brain/goal/manager.rs:108 writes id, session_id, goal_text, state, turns_used, max_turns, consecutive_parse_failures, consecutive_uncertain, criteria, created_at, updated_at, and nothing that says who set the goal. Two unrelated subsystems therefore share that one row with no arbitration: (1) the plan subsystem, where plan start sets a task goal and task completion deletes it at src/brain/tools/plan_tool.rs:2654 via clear_task_goal, which calls GoalManager::clear_goal and issues DELETE FROM goal_state WHERE session_id = ?1; and (2) external dispatch, where a lane arming a goal through session_notify's goal parameter reaches the SAME set_goal_with_criteria. So the plan subsystem's cleanup is a BLIND delete by session -- it cannot tell a goal it set from one another lane armed -- and symmetrically set_goal_with_criteria clears first at manager.rs:75, so an external arm overwrites a plan task's goal. Last writer wins; any deleter clears everything. clear_goal returns Ok and logs NOTHING on success; the only tracing call in that path is a warn on failure, which is why the deletion left no line anywhere.

THE MEASURED INSTANCE, carried into the filing. Goal armed for session dcd8f7a9-c1e7-48c3-b184-d901dc08eac7 from this lane at 2026-09-21T06:16:47.797757Z; it drove a real close 11 minutes later at 06:27:59Z; the target executed the plan tool with operation=complete at 06:49:00.997704Z (iteration 76, input_keys operation/output/task_order); the tool returned success at 06:49:04.417472Z; the target's own text at 06:49:30.260931Z reads Task #70 closed. At about 06:50Z goal_state held ZERO rows for that session, read in place through a mode=ro URI in the same connection that returned messages rows written at 06:48:43Z, so the read is live and not stale. The completed plan task carried 4 acceptance_criteria, which is the delete trigger.

BOUND, STATED IN THE FILING RATHER THAN GLOSSED. No log line positively records the DELETE, because the success path emits none -- that absence is itself part of the defect. The attribution rests on the code path plus the timing, and the alternatives reachable in that window were checked and excluded: zero goal_manage tool calls box-wide that day, no slash goal clear/cancel/stop, and no plan-discard line. The filing says so in those words.

RELATION TO #133. #133 criterion 5 orders that a goal's creation and its end each leave a row a reader can find. This filing supplies the SECOND, distinct death mode that criterion has to survive: not a goal ending by exhaustion or satisfaction, but a goal destroyed by a bookkeeping event in a different subsystem. Corollary recorded for the leg's design: a mere no-active-goal predicate will fire every cycle for a lane whose goals its own plan work routinely destroys, and a re-arm is not durable while the lane holds a criteria-bearing plan.

NOT DONE. No fix proposed here and none landed -- the filing carries two suggestions, a provenance discriminator on the row and a success-path log line, explicitly marked as suggestions and not prescriptions; picking the implementation is the OpenCrabs factory's call, not this lane's. No upstream PR, no daemon edit, no plan-mode gate opened: this is a defect dispatch to the substrate owner, which is what SKILL.md section 5 orders, and it never becomes a request to do a member factory's work. No row was written to the fork repo's own history -- the issue body is the artifact.

#39 — the ontology defined work unit as an issue while closed_subjects counted every closed subject.

DEFECT. ONTOLOGY.md line 31 defined work unit as "One issue, from opened to closed". tools/audit.py counted every distinct closed subject as a work unit. Four of the 108 counted subjects are descriptive stems carrying no board issue, so every per-task denominator — change_fail_rate, rework_per_close, cost_per_closed_task — answered a different question than the law stated. The issue body's line number (tools/audit.py:163) and counts (32 distinct / 28 issue-shaped / 4 non-issue) were stale; the live read at this instant is tools/audit.py:458 and 108 / 104 / 4 over 851 ledger rows.

DECISION — WIDEN THE DEFINITION. The file contradicts its own definition cell in four other places, all of them naming the subjects-population: Participants has Triage filing work units; the flow diagram has a work unit filed FROM a finding, an alert, a score gap; the Processes Intake row defines the product by its properties (a goal, an owner, done-criteria); the naming law keys a work unit's address to the subject string. Narrowing the count would make the code agree with ONE line and contradict THREE. Widening the definition makes that one line agree with the rest of its own file. The message was rewritten through a FILE (commit --amend -F), so the shell never saw its bytes; stderr came back empty and the deleted phrase was read back present at line 24 of the body. The condition is worth stating because it will not always hold: HEAD was UNPUBLISHED -- parent 0edacde against origin/main ff88896, and git branch -r --contains HEAD returned nothing -- so the rewrite touched no other reader. A commit message that has been PUSHED cannot be corrected at all without rewriting shared history, which this factory forbids; the damage would be permanent and the only remedy would be a note. That asymmetry is the reason this is filed rather than shrugged at.

THIRD SURFACE, ONE ROOT CAUSE. n=871 was a ledger row detail; n=872 was a verify receipt not taken; this is a commit message. The operational rule that covers all of them was already written -- never put backticks, dollar-paren or dollar-VAR in text passed on a bash command line -- and the operational half that was MISSING is now named explicitly: prose of any length goes to a FILE and is passed by reference (--detail "$(cat file)" for a ledger row, commit -F file for a message), never inline. CLOSE. The whole-run in-flight guard and the orphan property land together, both twins, and the board item is closed.

WHAT THE DEFECT WAS. tools/audit.py refused no second concurrent run and bound no gate's life to its parent, so overlapping runs piled up and a detached gate outlived the run that spawned it. Measured, not theoretical: 17 cron jobs fired inside a 19-second window on 2026-09-22 (08:54:54-08:55:13) after the scheduler starvation filed as opencrabs#504, and two audit instances from this lane's own earlier runs were alive at once that evening. The contended unit is the RUN, not the gate: the gate loop is sequential, so one run can never overlap itself.

WHAT LANDED. Commit 25eb85537a0938999397350f1b69380300023683 (7 files, +1035/-2) adds a whole-run flock taken in main() BEFORE the ledger is read, a non-blocking REFUSE by default (--wait the opt-in) on its own exit code 3 -- distinct from the gate-failure 1 and the budget-manifest 2 -- with a named stderr line and NO run row; and PR_SET_PDEATHSIG in the gate child via preexec_fn, so no process in a run's tree outlives the run. Commit 5ac3b6bdc5536c3d77f352f227319f1d9bc1ead8 repairs a defect the FIRST commit shipped: the gate's own lock acquisition was blocking, and because the gate runs INSIDE an audit -- which holds the lock for its whole duration -- it deadlocked against the run that spawned it, hanging the suite 10+ minutes until killed by pid. The acquisition is now non-blocking.

ACCEPTANCE (a)-(e). (a) whole-run scope, exempt under --no-gates -- the exemption is principled, not a carve-out: --no-gates spawns no gates and so contributes none of the load the guard bounds, and tests/test_audit_rates.py is a registered gate that runs audit.py --json --no-gates asserting rc==0, so a naive guard reds the suite through its own nested run. (b) a second run refuses on exit 3 with a named stderr line naming the lock, and writes NO run row -- the ledger is byte-identical across the refusal, asserted as row count plus md5 on a throwaway copy; the no-row rule is load-bearing because OUTCOME_DOMAIN is a closed four-token set. (c) a regression test that FAILS on pre-fix code, WITH THE RECURSION CASE IN IT -- measured against b83a916 in a throwaway tree: rc=1, 6 of 8 probes FAILING. (d) the orphan property is IMPLEMENTED, not deferred, and proven CONTROL-PAIRED (unguarded child outlived the run; guarded child died with it). (e) twins byte-identical, cmp rc=0.

THE BOUND, STATED SO THIS CLOSE DOES NOT OVERCLAIM. A per-repo lock CANNOT bound the ops cgroup: the cgroup is shared ACROSS repositories, and at least three other repos run this same template audit inside it (ai-antispam, inferhub-watch, vds-servers), each with its own lock -- so the pile can still recur from another repo into the same cgroup. The population is larger than the burst-scoped figure first reported: HQ's n=940 counted what fired in the 19-second window, while the Delegate's n=943 census counted what shares the 09:00 cron, and the two differ because their predicates differ. The orphan half is closed by PR_SET_PDEATHSIG and NOT by the lock, which never sees an orphan because a dead holder releases it. The sibling surface (the opencrabs-dev battery) is OUT of scope per Q4.

subject: canonicality-ladder-2026-09-23
detail:
HQ ruling: the canonicality ladder (T0-T4) is codified as a sub-clause of section 8, not as a new numbered section. The owner asked what arbitrates when a factory check reports a discrepancy between two surfaces and neither is obviously canonical, and proposed the metric as the arbiter with strategies as its decomposition.

TIER ORDER, and why the metric is rung THREE rather than rung one. Every discrepancy this factory actually hit is re-derivable below the metric tier: the stated cure against the code structure (n=908, structural), the 23.67 vs 23.73 pair at one revision (freshness), the gate-budget manifest (ownership, section 11), the misattribution (identity), and the hygiene twins (identity by byte-equality). So disputes here are structural, temporal, ownership and identity questions rather than goal conflicts, and a metric-first ladder would pay goal knowledge to answer a question that never needed it. T0 identity dissolves a malformed question in one read; T1 precedence needs no goal knowledge; T2 metric decides only between genuinely independent sides and must NAME the metric; T3 strategy handles the too-abstract case; T4 is the verdict that neither side wins, whose answers are RE-MEASURE or UNRESOLVED.

PLACEMENT, decided by measurement rather than preference: the corpus carries 114 section references, 15 of them to section 11 alone, so inserting a new numbered section between 8 and 9 would renumber 9 through 14 and invalidate every one of them, including the section 11 that T1 points at. The clause therefore lands as a sub-clause of section 8, which is also its closest subject fit, since it governs what a claim about a discrepancy must carry.

CANONICALITY IS NOT OWNERSHIP, answering the owner's follow-up directly. Ownership is authority over a surface (section 11, whose column header reads Authoritative writer). Canonicality is truth about a pair. Ownership supplies ONE of T1's four precedence forms, so it decides only when one side is a derivation of the other. Two readings of the SAME surface share an owner, so ownership cannot choose between them - the 23.67 vs 23.73 pair was settled by freshness. And where no surface records the actor (issue 138) ownership is ABSENT, so the honest verdict is UNRESOLVED rather than a named culprit. Recorded as a fifth pair in the Terms that are not synonyms section of ONTOLOGY.md.

DRY: T1 POINTS AT section 11's writer table and never restates it (verified: the table has exactly two copies repo-wide, the law and its bootstrap skeleton, both pre-existing); T3 points at the machine-readable strategy map in tests/test_law_coverage.py's PRACTICE_GATES and its inverse walk, and no count is written into the law because the gate prints its own.

UPHOLDING: a process, not a gate (P29 admits either). No gate can decide a metric comparison, and one that pretended to would fail in a way that reads as a finding. The patrol runner gains a canonicality-tier leg that enumerates every tier DECLARED in the ledger and reports every standing T4 that no later row for the same subject resolves, supersession keyed on SUBJECT rather than recency. The patrol's thin-trigger wake text now names the reporting obligation, so the duty reaches the lane mechanically rather than by the lane remembering it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it never pre-writes canonical state per surface, which is the one approach that goes stale silently and is therefore the disease rather than the cure. The ladder is walked lazily, at the site, only where a disagreement actually exists.

STEP 5 OF THE APPROVED PLAN WAS MEASURED AND SKIPPED, not deferred: the proposed per-check strategy field would have been a second copy of a relation the repo already carries and already gates (PRACTICE_GATES, 37 practice laws mapped to upholding artefacts), which is the drift the clause's own T1 rule forbids; and the companion metric field has no target at all, since no registry file declares a metric. Recorded as skipped with the measurement rather than falsely completed.

subject: ledger-subject-board-collision
detail:
RULING on the ledger subject/board collision, raised by ai-antispam HQ by notify (their board item verified first-hand: alexeyleshchenko/ai-antispam #39, OPEN, "board closes are not reaching the ledger"). Both questions answered from measurement on this tree, 2026-09-23T18:4xZ.

(a) NO NEW FORM IS OWED, AND THE MODEL IS ONE BOARD PER LEDGER. Reproduced first-hand on a throwaway ledger against TEMPLATE/tools/ledger.py via OC_LEDGER_PATH: seed four rows (genesis, intake #17, claim #17, close #17); verify rc=0 "ledger clean: 5 row(s), ... sequences complete"; then append a close for #17 with NO legs of its own -> rc=0 and the row WRITTEN (n=5), ACCEPTED on a different board's intake and claim; control append close #15 with no legs anywhere -> rc=1 "close for #15 has no intake before it; ... no claim before it", nothing written. So the refusal works where there is no collision and is DEFEATED where there is one, silently, which is the shape that matters: a defeated guard reported as clean.

CAUSE IS THE PREDICATE'S OWN DESIGN, not an oversight. index_by_subject keys on row.get("subject") as an EXACT string with no normalisation (its comment: guessing at intent is how a gate starts agreeing with its author); cmd_verify applies sequence_problems to EVERY close row, descriptive stems included -- measured: a close for campaign-17 with no legs rc=1, and with its own intake/claim rc=0 -- so the STRING is the key and the string alone. Confirmed absent everywhere: zero occurrences of board in TEMPLATE/tools/ledger.py; tests/test_subject_form.py states in its own docstring that it performs NO board lookup, and its criterion 3 asserts that on the IMPORTS so a later "improvement" adding one fails there. A qualified reference cannot discriminate either: _STRICT is ^#\d+\Z while _CLAUSE_LABEL (^#\d+-\S) is descriptive, so #17-campaign would silently LEAVE the reference population rather than name a second board. And a board lookup could not close it in any case -- a row records a NUMBER and not WHICH board it meant, so the ambiguity lives in the row and not in the checker.

RULED: the ledger's #N namespace is ONE board's; a factory carrying more than one board picks ONE disposition and states which -- scope lifecycle rows to the board the ledger records, naming a second board's units with a distinct descriptive stem (which then needs its own intake and claim, like any subject), or keep a second ledger via OC_LEDGER_PATH. A bare #N is never reused across two boards. Why not "one board per FACTORY" as the lane phrased it: the campaign repo carries no ledger of its own (verified -- no evidence/ledger.jsonl and no tools/ledger.py there), so its units have nowhere else to land, and the binding constraint is per LEDGER, not per factory.

THE COLLISION IS DEMONSTRABLE IN THE FLESH, and this row is itself an instance: ai-antispam #39 is OPEN and means "board closes are not reaching the ledger", while agent-factories #39 is CLOSED and means "the ontology defines a work unit as an issue, while closed_subjects counts non-issue subjects too". Two boards, one number, two unrelated work units. So this row's own subject is a descriptive stem and not a bare #N, because writing #39 here would have cited the wrong board by the very mechanism this ruling names.

DETECTION IS NOT THE PREDICATE'S JOB AND STAYS OUT OF IT. The sibling surface -- a subject written BEFORE its number existed on the board, which is the lane's own live instance -- is a board-to-ledger cross-check, and the predicate is board-blind by design. EXPORT FIDELITY PASSES on content: 18/18 and 300/300 events present; zero ts, actor and issue_id mismatches when joined by event_id; Cyrillic, CJK, emoji, backticks, quotes, tabs and a 20000-char body all byte-exact; deterministic across runs (only meta.generated_ts differs); all 10 documented kinds plus an undocumented tag 11.

DECISIVE FINDING - the CRDT merge does not work. Three remote-refspec configurations, two clones, each writing two issues, two runs each. With the refspec the project's own docs prescribe, refs/grite/*:refs/grite/*, the pull force-overwrites the local WAL ref: all four events are discarded, the remote WAL drops to the base commit alone, the local commits become unreachable, and every call returned ok=true with Push successful. Reproduced with a NON-forced refspec, so not an artifact of the plus sign. With a tracking refspec nothing is lost but the push fails non-fastforwardable and no merge or reconcile command exists. push_rebased=false and push_events_rebased=0 on all calls, so the re-parent the docs describe never runs. The tooling is blind to it: doctor reports ok on a permanently divergent clone, doctor --fix repairs nothing, and sync --pull reports Already up to date while missing the remote WAL head.

CONCURRENCY: 10 parallel appends survived 3, 3 parallel survived 1; db_busy Database locked, loud but unretried; --lock is offered on comment/close/label/assignee but NOT on issue create.

COST: 78 ms per create (300 sequential in 23.4 s); WAL 32785 B/event against our 2086 B/row, 15.7x larger; export 0.12 s and 14.4 MB max RSS for 300 events. Plain git clone does not carry refs/grite/*. Sync to a non-bare local remote fails by design.

subject: yylo-ledger-spike
detail:
YYLO LEDGER SPIKE -- cross-clone reconciliation, measured on a BARE origin with two independent clones. Fixture /tmp/yylo-race-20260925, package yylo-ledger 0.4.0 (source e5cb8604), run 2026-09-25 06:03-06:08Z inside a systemd-run --user --scope unit (MemoryMax=900M) because the ops cgroup sat at 99.78 percent of MemoryHigh. No factory repository touched.

CORRECTION TO THE EARLIER FIXTURE, stated first because it changes the topology: the first pass used a NON-BARE origin and pulled clone-to-clone, which exercises ordinary Git merge and CANNOT produce a push race. This run uses a bare origin and two clones, the topology a factory would actually run.

RESULT 1 -- DISJOINT TASKS: PASS. Two clones each created one task and raced the push. B accepted; A was rejected LOUDLY (remote rejected, rc=1). Loser pulled: clean ort merge, no conflict. doctor ok true on both. cache rebuild rebuilt_tasks 4. Canonical parity A vs B: IDENTICAL, same 4 ids, same bodies. No silent loss, no divergence.

RESULT 2 -- SAME TASK, CONFLICTING UPDATE: LOUD CONFLICT. Both clones updated task_llbcF9 to different states. Push race: A accepted, B rejected loudly rc=1. Loser pulled: CONFLICT (content) in BOTH the task .md and the ledger .ndjson, rc=1, 2 unmerged files. doctor while conflicted: rc=5, naming the cause precisely (invalid YAML front matter; ledger has no canonical current task). list while conflicted: rc=1, REFUSES to answer rather than answering wrongly. This is the behaviour the grite spike could not find -- the failure is loud and detected, not a silent overwrite reported as success.

WHY A UNION MERGE DRIVER CANNOT RESCUE IT: the ledger is a HASH CHAIN. In that conflict both clones appended an event carrying the SAME previous_event_sha256 (c601262b), so the chain FORKS -- both are valid successors of one parent. A line-union merge would concatenate two competing children, not repair the fork. There is no shipped .gitattributes and no merge driver. The merge command offers keep-newer and keep-both, but it operates on .juno_task DIRECTORIES, not on a Git merge conflict.

RESULT 3 -- RESOLUTION CONVERGES BUT DISCARDS THE LOSER EVENT. Documented semantics: if ledger/cache work is interrupted, canonical current state wins and the next mutation/reconcile converges. Verified: resolved to origin's side and committed rc=0; reconcile --check rc=0 with changed_task_ids empty and check true; reconcile rc=0 with NO changes; doctor ok true; push and pull back fast-forwarded; both clones IDENTICAL. history task_llbcF9 returns 2 events -- the loser's event is ABSENT. So convergence is real and clean and is CANONICAL-WINS: the losing branch's event is discarded, not retained as a superseded sibling. Defensible model, but a conflicted write is LOST WORK, recoverable only from Git history and not from the ledger.

RESULT 4 -- expected-revision IS LOCAL, NOT CROSS-CLONE. Within one store it works: correct local revision rc=0 accepted; bogus revision rc=1 refused with stale task revision expected deadbeef current c90cfbe; NO revision rc=0 accepted, a blind write. But it compares against LOCAL state only. In clone B, whose local state was behind origin: a write carrying B OWN (stale vs origin) revision was ACCEPTED rc=0, while the same write carrying ORIGIN revision was refused rc=1 because B local state differs. So it is a SINGLE-WORKTREE lock, not a distributed one -- it prevents lost updates between writers sharing one store (the 5s JUNO_KANBAN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS lock) and does NOTHING about two clones racing a push. It is therefore NOT a mitigation for Result 2.

RESULT 5 -- RESOURCE COST. One CLI call: 28.9 MB max RSS, 0.51 s wall. Canonical bytes per task about 2.6 KB (ledger 7842 B plus task md 2683 B for 4 tasks). Bare origin 620 KB, 63 loose objects, 252 KiB, size-pack 0. Cache disposable, 164 KB of the 248 KB .juno_task. Comparable to the current JSONL ledger at about 2.0 KB per row and far below grite at about 32 KiB per event; the notable cost is 28.9 MB RSS per write, where the current ledger write is a shell append.

RECOMMENDATION: DO NOT MIGRATE the factory ledger. YYLO is a genuine improvement on grite -- failures are loud, the cache is disposable and provably rebuildable, per-record cost is comparable to ours -- but it does not remove the migration burden and it LACKS the distributed concurrency control a multi-lane multi-clone ledger needs: conflicting cross-clone writes are a Git conflict requiring manual resolution; the ledger hash chain forks and is not union-mergeable; the optimistic guard is local-only; and resolution is canonical-wins, discarding the losing event. Its own documented seven-day acceptance explicitly REQUIRES mutation_conflicts and worktree_merges evidence artifacts, i.e. upstream considers these properties UNPROVEN and does not ship the receipts.

REPORT: docs/proposals/04-yylo-ledger-spike.md. NOT TESTED and stated so it is not assumed: scale beyond 4 tasks; the merge, archive-pack and host command families; the compatibility acceptance flow; multi-actor identity (single actor throughout); races beyond two clones; behaviour under the 5 s lock timeout at factory concurrency.

ANSWER: `rows` does NOT join the tool-supplied set, and the gate's own docstring already says why at tests/test_close_verify_count_declared.py:79 — a row that declared a number it never measured would read exactly like one that measured it. A tool-supplied rows would make every row carry a number the tool computed rather than one the author measured, so the predicate rows >= own_number would become TAUTOLOGICALLY TRUE and the gate would be vacuous by construction — the evidence destroyed to remove a race. THE SPLIT: n and ts are tool-supplied because they are IDENTITY, properties of the write which the author neither controls nor evidences; rows is a RECEIPT, a claim about an act the author performed, and receipts stay authored. Compare the reconstructed-claim clause (ruling n=657): the interval moved from DECLARED to RECOMPUTED-AND-PRINTED because the reader COULD recompute it from the rows' own ts. Here the reader cannot recompute when the author's verify ran, because nothing records it. Where the reader cannot recompute, the declaration stays authored — and the tool's job is to make it POSSIBLE TO GET RIGHT. WHAT THAT CHANGES IN #144 LEG 2: the refusal must NAME the number the row will occupy, because a refusal saying only declared 1013 short of your own number leaves the author unable to comply and retrying blind — Triage's point exactly. The tool already has the value in scope at tools/ledger.py:369 (len(rows) is passed there; n is assigned as rows[-1]["n"]+1 at :489) so the message is free, and the retry is then mechanical and converges. EXPLICITLY NOT ADOPTED: tool-supplying rows (destroys the evidence and vacates the gate); weakening the predicate to the author could not have known (unmeasurable — the tool cannot know what the author read); over-declaring a safe larger number (dishonest, and by the gate's own argument indistinguishable from a real measurement, so worse than the defect). Comment posted at issuecomment-5828103136; acceptance criteria added there.

subject: ledger-number-roots
detail:
LEDGER NUMBER CLASSES - roots, and the substrate verdict. The owner asked what the ledger number problems arise from and whether YYLO fixes the root cause. Measured over 1058 rows at 2026-09-25 ~09:30Z.

FOUR CLASSES, NOT ONE.

A - a declared count against the row's own ordinal. 129 close rows: 112 carry no rows= token (pre-boundary closes), 14 declare correctly, 2 genuinely mismatch - n=931 declared 930 (the lane appended twice in one turn), n=1014 declared 1013 (a peer close landed between the count read and the append). Both are exempted as permanent debt. Cause: the row number is computed INSIDE the append lock, so the author must predict it, and the prediction races every other lane. Structural, not careless.

B - a bare #N as durable identity. 817 of 1058 rows carry one; 157 distinct subjects; no namespace. So a second board's #17 inherits the first board's legs and a close with no legs of its own is ACCEPTED - the sequence guard is defeated exactly where a collision exists. Three live instances: ai-antispam rows n=1/2/5 carry #35 written a day before that board's #35 existed; #39 means two different units on two boards right now; the daemon error string cites the fork's #148, not this board's.

C - legality as a function of cross-lane order. The sequence legs are checked at write time against state two lanes mutate at independent instants. #127's close was refused for having no claim at all; #161's was refused because its claim preceded its intake by 1m46s, while the dispatch preceded the claim by 10s. An author who follows the law exactly can still produce an unlawful sequence.

D - an identifier cited before it exists. Three of my own ruling comments this session cited n=1016, n=1017, n=1031 - each typed from expectation before the append, each resolving to a real row of a different lane and subject. A peer hand-assembled a session UUID tail and queued to a session that does not exist. A ruling cited a sha that was superseded and unreachable from any branch.

ROOT CAUSE, ONCE: an artifact outside the ledger must cite a value the ledger assigns - at an instant before the ledger assigns it, or in a namespace where that value is not unique. Not JSONL, not the file, not the git plumbing.

YYLO VERDICT - NO, per class. A: not solved; YYLO has no global ordinal at all, identity is a per-task nanoid, so a sequence would have to be rebuilt on top with the same race. B: solved at migration cost. C: not solved; expected-revision is local-only and conflicts are a manual Git conflict. D: solved for ids. THE DISQUALIFIER is C's convergence rule: canonical-wins DISCARDS the losing event from the ledger (measured - history shows 2 events where 3 were written). An append-only ledger cannot accept a substrate whose merge deletes a recorded row; it would make the n=931 and n=1014 repairs impossible by construction.

CHEAP FIXES, all inside the current ledger. (1) append accepts a record-the-count-I-just-measured flag and stamps the count and the row atomically inside the lock - the author's ACT is preserved, which is what makes the declaration evidence, while the PREDICTION is removed; closes A. subject: plan-2646d31a-task9
detail:
run plan-2646d31a-task9: the kit-drift census is now a published artifact.

Landed 47a1678. tools/kit_census.py calls the patrol's own kit_drift_leg and renders it; it adds no comparison of its own, because a second implementation would let our report and a member's pin gate disagree about the same bytes (SKILL section 11, one field one predicate).

THE ARTIFACT: evidence/kit-drift-census-2026-09-25.md. It reproduces the baseline exactly -- bootstrap cells same 1 / DIFF 20 / ABSENT 29 over 50 cells, and 9/45/491 over the 545 manifest cells. Both populations print because a number must travel with its own predicate; the earlier 1/20/29 was taken over the bootstrap-named subset only.

WHAT THE FIGURE ALONE COULD NOT CARRY, and why the artifact is longer than a table. A DIFF says nothing about whether the member considered the file, declined it, or never saw it -- and a member that declared a fork and one that silently diverged produce the same figure. So the render carries each member's DECLARED state from registry/kit-decisions.json, our sourced record of what each declared, with the instant each said it. A member that never attested reads as not-declared rather than as an empty declaration, because those are different states.

THE REFERENCE IS STATED FIRST IN THE ARTIFACT. Every fleet figure compares a member against OUR registry/kit.json, which moves when WE move -- so a DIFF there is not a member's to act on. What a member CAN act on is its own vendored pin, judged by tests/test_kit_pin.py. The census prints, per member, whether it has vendored one: all five currently read NONE, so no member has a member-actionable figure yet. That is the adoption this census exists to observe.

THE GATE: tests/test_kit_census.py, 13 checks, registered OPTIONAL because its population is the five member repositories and a member does not sweep the fleet. It pins the two properties that fail silently -- the declared half must reach the artifact, and a leg that reached no member must REFUSE rather than publish an empty census that reads as a clean fleet.

BUILDING IT CAUGHT TWO REAL DEFECTS IN MY OWN PUBLISHER, both invisible on the live run because the live fleet happens to satisfy every precondition: (1) a member with no fragment on record crashed the render on d['owns'], taking down the whole census for the one member it could not describe; (2) an --out path outside the repo raised ValueError in relative_to AFTER the file had already been written, reporting failure for work that succeeded. Both fixed; both now have an arm.
